newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco battles locust invasion in Western Sahara.
newsitem.headline: Morocco battles locust invasion in Western Sahara.

text.p: Morocco is battling a locust invasion with swarms covering 4,000 hectares (10,000 acres) in the Western Sahara's regions of Mahbes, Dakhla and Boujdour, the official MAP news agency said on Friday.
"Anti-locust units were reinforced by helicopters and anti-locust plan already in place has been recently strenghtened," said MAP.
The disputed Western Sahara is under Moroccan administration since 1976 after the former Spanish colonial ruler withdrew from the desert territory calimed by the Algeria-backed Polisario guerrillas.
The last major locust was in 1988 when the souther rich Souss valley crops, particularly export-proned citrus groves, were ravaged.
